observations: The page number «235» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. At the foot, the signature «30*» on the right; recorded here, not transcribed as a line. L01 continues the sentence of p. 234 (JP2 0266, L37).

L08: the formula is displayed in a line of its own, centred, the fraction built up, written {fr:NUMERATOR|DENOMINATOR}; r and ψ in italics, as «RET» in L05. L28-L32: the table of the mean motions, in columns: in L29-L31 a long dash under «Mittellauf» and a short one under «in» stand for the repeated words, and a long dash under «Tagen» in L29; a rule across the table above L32; «365d 6h 12m» (L32, L33) with the letters raised, «9s» (L37) likewise; the values as printed, «348°54′13″» without spaces and «360° 0′ 0″» with them. Here the cells separated by our «|»; a cell followed by empty cells spans their columns.

L28-L32. Checked: the motions are those of the tables of the mean sun: one single Arab year of 354 days 11s 18° 54′ 13″ = 348° 54′ 13″ (Tab. 4, p. 115, JP2 0147), 11 days 10° 50′ 30″, 6 hours 14′ 47″ and 12 parts of an hour 30″ (Tab. 5, p. 116, JP2 0148); their sum is 360° 0′ 0″ exactly, so the sun returns to its place in 365d 6h 12m. On p. 42 (JP2 0074, L08-L13) Suter had 12 · 29° 34′ 5″ = 354° 49′ for 360 days and 365d 6h 13m. The 6h 12m agree with the 6h 12m 9s of the year of Tab. 115 (p. 230, JP2 0262).

L01-L08. Checked with r, the radius of the epicycle, taken as the sine of the greatest equation of the anomaly of each planet in the tables (Tab. 27-56, pp. 138-167, JP2 0170-0199; the printed misprints of p. 149 and p. 167, critical notes AK07-CN130 and AK07-CN164, set aside): the equations of the anomaly agree with the formula of L08 within 4.1′ for Saturn and 6.4′ for Mercury, within 10.4′ for Jupiter and 11.9′ for Venus, the larger differences falling between 150° and 177°, and differ from it by up to 21.3′ for Mars, at 161°, the 21′ at 160°-170° of Pechüle (L03-L04).

L15-L17: on p. 48 (JP2 0080) the tenth line, L10, reads «genannt wurde, weil er aus dem Centrum des Aequans gemessen gedacht wird ; ferner», of the centre (al-markaz). L18-L21: «Panchasiddhāntikā» stands on p. 46 (JP2 0078, L29, N01) and elsewhere in the commentary, as Suter says. «Transskriptionsweise» (L19) and «Transskriptionsart» (L21) are spelled with ss twice; «Pan-chasiddhāntikā» (L19-L20) is divided at the end of the line, «Brahma-Siddhānta» (L37-L38) at its hyphen.

Spaced type, marked {sp:}: «Pechüle» (L01), «Kh.’s» (L02), «Kh.» (L04, L13, L33, L39), «Varāhamihira» (L18), «Thibaut» (L19), «Al-Bīrūnī» (L34); «Sachau» (L34) is not spaced. Italics: «RET», r, ψ, «Pan-chasiddhāntikā», «Pañcasiddhāntikā», «Brahma-Siddhānta», «Sindhind», «persischen», «Shāh». Bold: the numbers «2.», «3.», «4.». Dashes: «4′—5′», «160°—170°», «12—13» and «61—62» long (41-45 px, the third broken).
